Date: 2027-05-19T09:08:00-07:00
Subject: Sudden QPS drop & spikes in latency affecting checkout

Hi Avery,

We're seeing a significant drop in QPS to Redwood (about 40% below baseline) starting ~08:50 PDT and intermittent latency spikes up to 3.5s across gen endpoints. This is impacting checkout flows for a subset of users — conversion is down. We've attached a screenshot from our telemetry and a short export of request IDs around the impact window.

Can you confirm if this is on Redwood's side or anything we should change on our end? We're on model redwood/gpt-neo-14b-v2 (pinned) and routing through us-west.

Thanks — Claire
Claire Zhang

Thanks — triage notes so far (09:34 PDT):
1) No infra maintenance events recorded in us-west at 08:30–09:00.
2) Autoscaler logged several rapid instance terminations in pool-gp2-usw; investigating cause (OOM vs preemption).
3) Router logs show an increase in 503s for specific shards servicing the redwood/gpt-neo-14b-v2 variant between 08:48–09:05.
4) I've pulled kube/node metrics and starting a deeper inspection of kernel and serving-runtime traces; will escalate to runtime if we see abnormal kernel selection or failed kernel fallbacks.

Temporary mitigations in progress:
- Rebalanced traffic away from the 3 failing shards (manual reroute) — starting now.
- Increasing pool capacity on standby nodes to absorb load; ETA 15 minutes.

Next update: 09:55 PDT with either mitigation results or root-cause.

-Soojin
Soojin Lee
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>

Date: 2027-05-19T09:52:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Sudden QPS drop & spikes in latency affecting checkout

Quick engineering findings (runtime traces, 09:52 PDT):
- We observed kernel-selection thrashing for gpt-neo-14b-v2 on the affected shards: mixed use of a new int8 quant kernel that was rolled quietly in canary last week. The kernel's memory-access pattern increases tail latency under certain sequence-length distributions.
- When SRE rerouted traffic off the shards, p95/p99 latency returned toward baseline for those requests.
- Root cause hypothesis: combination of (a) a canary kernel rollout on a fraction of capacity and (b) a short-lived autoscaler churn that concentrated traffic on canary-enabled nodes.

Proposed immediate actions:
1) Pause the new int8 kernel on canary nodes (we can flip the feature flag) — target complete in 20 minutes.
2) Persist manual routing adjustments until autoscaler stabilizes (Soojin).
3) Run a targeted job to rebalance KV cache warmness after nodes come back to normal.

I'll prepare a short postmortem draft once we confirm mitigation.

-Vivek
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime

Avery — drafting a concise customer-facing note below. Please edit as needed; I want to be factual and minimize speculation.

DRAFT to MillerShop:

Hi Claire / Sam —

Thanks for flagging this. Quick update: our SRE and runtime teams detected an emergent failure pattern in a small set of serving shards in us-west that briefly reduced throughput and caused elevated tail latency for requests running gpt-neo-14b-v2. We have:
- Rerouted traffic from the affected shards to healthy capacity.
- Paused a recent kernel rollout that, in combination with autoscaler activity, increased tail latency for certain request patterns.
- Brought standby capacity up to handle load and rebalanced traffic — monitoring shows recovery toward baseline.

Action items we are taking now:
- Run a cache-warm job to restore KV prefix warmness (reduces cold-token latency).
- Do a targeted sweep of recent kernel rollouts and add a preflight check to detect this pattern.
- Postmortem and timeline within 48 hours.

We're attaching telemetry snapshots and the mitigation checklist. We'll update you at 11:30 PDT with progress; please let us know if you see ongoing customer impact.

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Customer Reliability Manager, Redwood Inference

Subject: Redwood update: mitigation in place & next steps (MillerShop)

Hi Claire / Sam —

Following up with a summary from our internal incident triage. TL;DR: we identified a canary kernel rollout combined with transient autoscaler churn that caused a concentration of traffic onto canary-enabled nodes; that combination produced higher tail latencies and reduced effective QPS for a small subset of requests.

What we did (completed):
- Manually rerouted traffic off the three affected shards and increased standby capacity (completed 05/19 10:05 PDT).
- Paused the int8 canary kernel rollout and rolled back the kernel flag on canary nodes (completed 05/19 10:20 PDT).
- Executed a KV cache rewarm job and monitored token-level latencies; metrics indicate recovery toward baseline within ~30 minutes of mitigation.

What we're doing next (short term):
- Full postmortem with timeline and corrective actions within 48 hours.
- Add a preflight rollout check that simulates sequence-length distributions common to MillerShop before enabling kernels for production traffic.
- Offer a short credits package for the impacted window; I'll coordinate with our finance team if you'd like to pursue.

We appreciate the heads-up and apologize for the disruption. Please let us know if you still observe elevated latencies or if you want us to pause any future rollouts for your pinned model until we finish the postmortem.

—Avery
Avery Johnson
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
